The planned merger of two major streaming platforms, HBO Max and Paramount+, may ultimately not come to fruition.

The plan was announced in March this year after Netflix withdrew from the bidding war to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary injunction blocking the deal from being completed—at least for now……

The original merger plan

The deal involves Paramount acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery, with its streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ to be integrated into a single service.

Temporary injunction

Viewers are not particularly enthusiastic about the plan, fearing it would reduce competition and drive up prices. A coalition of attorneys general from 12 states shares the same view and has petitioned a federal court to issue a temporary injunction on the deal. According to NBC News, the injunction has been granted.

The injunction is valid for 14 days, pending arguments from both sides. Even if Paramount wins the case, the merger plan will still be subject to review by the European Union and the UK government. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, alleging that the merger would lead to job losses and pay cuts.
